1544:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate or possess a UAS that is equipped with:
(1) A destructive device;
(2) Any modification that has not been approved by the FAA; or
(3) Any substance defined as a controlled substance under the Georgia Controlled Substances Act (O.C.G.A. § 16-13-20).
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a UAS while under the influence of alcohol, a controlled substance, or any drug, prescription or otherwise, that impairs the operator's ability to safely operate the UAS. For purposes of this section, a person is considered under the influence if they:
(1) Have a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.04 percent or higher while operating a UAS;
(2) Are impaired to the extent that physical or mental faculties are noticeably diminished; or
(3) Are under the influence of any controlled substance as defined by state or federal law, without lawful prescription or authorization.
(c) It shall be unlawful for any person to recklessly engage in conduct involving a UAS.
(d) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a UAS in a manner that creates a public nuisance. A public nuisance includes, but is not limited to, operations that unreasonably disturb the peace, invade personal privacy, interfere with lawful public activities or gatherings, or otherwise cause annoyance or alarm to members of the public.
(e) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a UAS to intentionally engage in surveillance of another person when the other person is located in a private place.
(f) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a UAS in a manner that endangers, or creates an unreasonable risk of harm to, the safety, comfort, or property of another person. This includes, but is not limited to, operations conducted at unsafe altitudes, in proximity to people, animals, buildings, or vehicles, or in weather or conditions that impair the operator's ability to safely control the UAS.
(g) It shall be unlawful to operate a UAS in a manner that intentionally disturbs, chases, threatens, harasses, or otherwise interferes with the natural behavior or habitat of wildlife. This includes intentionally flying near, following, or causing flight responses in birds, mammals, or other protected species.
(h) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a UAS in a manner that interferes with, obstructs, or disrupts any active public safety operation. This includes, but is not limited to, law enforcement activities, firefighting efforts, emergency medical services, disaster response, search and rescue, or any other emergency or government response involving personnel, vehicles, or aircraft. Interference includes operating a UAS:
(1) Within a temporary flight restriction (TFR) established by the FAA;
(2) Within visual proximity to active public safety operations where the drone's presence distracts personnel or delays response;
(3) In a way that forces aircraft (e.g. helicopters or air ambulances) or public safety UAS to alter or suspend operations; or
(4) In a manner that violates FAA regulations related to emergency operations.
(i) It shall be unlawful to operate or possess a UAS that is painted, marked, or equipped in a manner that falsely represents the UAS as belonging to law enforcement, emergency services, or military entities, unless operated by such authorized personnel.
(j) It shall be unlawful to operate a UAS equipped with any other device or payload (e.g. Taser, signal jammer, biometric scanner) not expressly authorized by law that poses a threat to public safety, privacy, or civil order, as determined by the City or its designee.
(k) It shall be unlawful to operate a UAS beyond the visual line of sight of the operator or designated observer, unless such operation is authorized by a valid FAA waiver, certificate of waiver or authorization (COA), or other written approval from the FAA permitting such activity. Operations conducted solely through video feed, first-person view (FPV), or any onboard camera system do not satisfy this requirement without an accompanying FAA waiver.
(l) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a UAS during nighttime hours unless the operation is conducted in full compliance with applicable FAA regulations.
(m) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a UAS over people or open-air assemblies that are non-participants in the UAS flight operation, unless the operation is conducted in full compliance with applicable FAA regulations.

(9) Channel means a natural or artificial watercourse with a definite bed and banks that conveys continuously or periodically flowing water.

a. Owned or maintained by the City;
b. Not a combined sewer; and

(11) Clean Water Act means the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (33 USC 1251 et seq.), and any subsequent amendments thereto.
(12) Code means the Official Code of Georgia Annotated.
(13) Commission means the Georgia Soil and Water Conservation Commission (GSWCC).
(14) Common development means a contiguous area where multiple, separate, and distinct construction activities may be taking place at different times on different schedules under one plan of development or sale.
(15) Conservation easement means an agreement between a land owner and the City or other government agency or land trust that permanently protects open space or greenspace on the owner's land by limiting the amount and type of development that can take place, but continues to leave the remainder of the fee interest in private ownership.
(16) Construction activity means activities subject to the Georgia Erosion and Sedimentation Control Act or State general construction permits. The term "construction activity" includes construction projects resulting in land disturbance. Such activities include, but are not limited to, clearing and grubbing, grading, excavating and demolition.
(17) CPESC means certified professional in erosion and sediment control with current certification by EnviroCert, Inc., which is also referred to as CPESC or CPESC Inc.

(19) Department means the Georgia Department of Natural Resources (DNR).
(20) Design professional means a professional licensed by the State in the field of: engineering, architecture, landscape architecture, forestry, geology, or land surveying; or a person that is a certified professional in erosion and sediment control (CPESC) with a current certification by EnviroCert, Inc. Design professionals shall practice in a manner that complies with applicable State law governing professional licensure.
(21) Detention means the temporary storage of stormwater runoff in a stormwater detention facility for the purpose of controlling the peak discharge.
(22) Detention facility means a structure designed for the storage and gradual release of stormwater runoff at controlled rates.
(23) Developer means a person who undertakes land development activities.
(24) Development means new development or redevelopment.
(25) Director means the Director of the Environmental Protection Division or an authorized representative.
(26) District means the Rockdale County Soil and Water Conservation District.
(27) Division means the Environmental Protection Division (EPD) of the Department of Natural Resources.
(28) Drainage easement means an easement appurtenant or attached to a tract or parcel of land allowing the owner of adjacent tracts or other persons to discharge stormwater runoff onto the tract or parcel of land subject to the drainage easement.

(31) Erosion, sedimentation and pollution control plan means a plan required by the Erosion and Sedimentation Act (O.C.G.A. § 12-7-1 et seq.) that includes, as a minimum, protections at least as stringent as the State General Permit, best management practices, and requirements in Section 12-2-5.
(32) Extended detention means the storage of stormwater runoff for an extended period of time.
(33) Extreme flood protection means measures taken to prevent adverse impacts from large low-frequency storm events with a return frequency of 100 years or more.
(34) Fill means a portion of land surface to which soil or other solid material has been added; the depth above the original ground surface or an excavation.
(35) Final stabilization means all soil disturbing activities at the site have been completed, and that for unpaved areas and areas not covered by permanent structures and areas located outside the waste disposal limits of a landfill cell that has been certified by EPD for waste disposal, 100 percent of the soil surface is uniformly covered in permanent vegetation with a density of 70 percent or greater, or landscaped according to the plan (uniformly covered with landscaping materials in planned landscape areas), or equivalent permanent stabilization measures as defined in the manual (excluding a crop of annual vegetation and seeding of target crop perennials appropriate for the region). (36) Finished grade means the final elevation and contour of the ground after cutting or filling and conforming to the proposed design.
(37) Flooding means a volume of surface water that exceeds the banks or walls of a BMP, or channel; and overflows onto adjacent lands.

(a) The basin being fully developed as shown on the current land use plan; or
(b) The regulatory floodplain as defined by the National Flood Insurance Program (FEMA).
The more restrictive (wider) of either (a) or (b) shall be used.
(39) GSWCC means the Georgia Soil and Water Conservation Commission.
(40) GSMM means the latest edition of the Georgia Stormwater Management Manual, Volume 2: Technical Handbook, and its appendices.

(42) Greenspace or open space means permanently protected areas of the site that are preserved in a natural state.
(43) Ground elevation means the original elevation of the ground surface prior to cutting or filling.

(47) Illegal connection or illicit connection means either of the following:
a. Any pipe, open channel, drain or conveyance, whether on the surface or subsurface, which allows an illicit discharge to enter the City separate storm sewer system, including but not limited to any conveyance which allow any nonstormwater discharge including sewage, process wastewater, and wash water to enter the City separate storm sewer system, regardless of whether such pipe, open channel, drain or conveyance has been previously allowed, permitted, or approved by an authorized enforcement agency; or
b. Any pipe, open channel, drain or conveyance connected to the City separate storm sewer system, which has not been documented in plans, maps, or equivalent records and approved by an authorized enforcement agency.

(50) Industrial activity means activities subject to NPDES industrial permits as defined in 40 CFR 122.26(b)(14).

(54) Inspection and maintenance agreement means a written agreement providing for the long-term inspection, operation, and maintenance of the stormwater management system and its components on a site.

Wetlands generally include swamps, marshes, bogs, and similar areas.

(57) Land development activity means those actions or activities that comprise, facilitate or result in land development.

(65) Linear transportation projects means construction projects on traveled ways including but not limited to roads, sidewalks, multi-use paths and trails, and airport runways and taxiways.

(70) Natural ground surface means the ground surface in its original state before any grading, excavation or filling.

(78) O.C.G.A. means the Official Code of Georgia Annotated.

d. Petroleum and related hydrocarbons (such as fuels, lubricants, surfactants, waste oils, solvents, coolants, and grease);

g. h. Materials causing an increase in biochemical oxygen demand, chemical oxygen demand, or total organic carbon;

Subject to the applicability criteria in Section 12-4-2 and exemptions in Section 12-4-3, the following stormwater management standards apply. Additional details for each standard can be found in the GSMM Section 2.2.2.2:
(a) Design of stormwater management system. The design of the stormwater management system shall be in accordance with the applicable sections of the GSMM as directed by the administrator. Any design which proposes a dam shall comply with the Georgia Safe Dams Act and Rules for Dam Safety as applicable.
(b) Natural resources inventory. Site reconnaissance and surveying techniques shall be used to complete a thorough assessment of existing natural resources, both terrestrial and aquatic, found on the site. Resources to be identified, mapped, and shown on the stormwater management plan, shall include, at a minimum (as applicable):
(i) Topography (minimum of two-foot contours) and steep slopes (i.e. areas with slopes greater than 15 percent);
(ii) Natural drainage divides and patterns;
(iii) Natural drainage features (e.g. swales, basins, depressional areas);
(iv) Natural feature protection and conservation areas such as wetlands, lakes, ponds, floodplains, stream buffers, drinking water wellhead protection areas and river corridors;
(v) Predominant soils (including erodible soils and karst areas); and
(vi) Existing predominant vegetation including trees, high quality habitat and other existing vegetation.
(c) Better site design practices for stormwater management. Stormwater management plans shall preserve the natural drainage and natural treatment systems and reduce the generation of additional stormwater runoff and pollutants to the maximum extent practicable. Additional details can be found in the GSMM Section 2.3.
(d) Stormwater runoff quality/reduction. Stormwater runoff quality/reduction shall be provided by using the following:
(i) For development with a stormwater management plan submitted before December 6, 2020 the applicant may choose either (A) runoff reduction or (B) water quality.
(ii) For development with a stormwater management plan submitted on or after December 6, 2020, the applicant shall choose (A) runoff reduction and additional water quality shall not be required. To the extent (A) runoff reduction has been determined to be infeasible for all or a portion of the site using the practicability policy, then (B) water quality shall apply for the remaining runoff from a 1.2-inch rainfall event and must be treated to remove at least 80 percent of the calculated average annual post-development total suspended solids (TSS) load or equivalent as defined in the GSMM.
(A) Runoff reduction. The stormwater management system shall be designed to retain the first one inch of rainfall on the site using runoff reduction methods, to the maximum extent practicable.
(B) Water quality. The stormwater management system shall be designed to remove at least 80 percent of the calculated average annual post-development total suspended solids (TSS) load or equivalent as defined in the GSMM for runoff from a 1.2-inch rainfall event.
(iii) If a site is determined to be a hotspot as detailed in Section 12-4-5, the City may require the use of specific or additional components for the stormwater management system to address pollutants of concern generated by that site.
(e) Stream channel protection. Stream channel protection shall be provided by using all of the following three approaches:
(i) 24-hour extended detention storage of the one-year, 24-hour return frequency storm event;
(ii) Erosion prevention measures, such as energy dissipation and velocity control; and
(iii) Preservation of any applicable stream buffer.
(f) Overbank flood protection. Downstream overbank flood protection shall be provided by controlling the post-development peak discharge rate to the pre-development rate for the 25-year, 24-hour storm event.
(g) Extreme flood protection. Extreme flood protection shall be provided by controlling the 100-year, 24-hour storm event such that flooding is not exacerbated.
(h) Downstream analysis. Due to peak flow timing and runoff volume effects, some structural components of the stormwater management system fail to reduce discharge peaks to pre-development levels downstream from the site. A downstream peak flow analysis shall be provided to the point in the watershed downstream of the site or the stormwater management system where the area of the site comprises ten percent of the total drainage area in accordance with Section 3.1.9 of the GSMM. This is to help ensure that there are minimal downstream impacts from development on the site. The downstream analysis may result in the need to resize structural components of the stormwater management system.
(i) Stormwater management system inspection and maintenance. The components of the stormwater management system that will not be dedicated to and accepted by the City, including all drainage facilities, best management practices, credited conservation spaces, and conveyance systems, shall have an inspection and maintenance agreement to ensure that they continue to function as designed. All new development and redevelopment sites are to prepare a comprehensive inspection and maintenance agreement for the on-site stormwater management system. This plan shall be written in accordance with the requirements in Section 12-4-15.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 2, 11-18-2020)

Land development applications are handled as part of the process to obtain the land disturbance permit pursuant to Title 12, Chapter 4 or building permit Title 8 Chapter 2, as applicable. (a) File a land development application with the City on the City's form of application with the following supporting materials:
(i) The stormwater management plan prepared in accordance with Section 12-4-8(d);
(ii) A certification that the development will be performed in accordance with the stormwater management plan once approved;
(iii) A preliminary determination of infeasibility, as applicable, prepared in accordance with the practicability policy; and
(iv) An acknowledgement that applicant has reviewed the City's form of inspection and maintenance agreement and that applicant agrees to sign and record such inspection and maintenance agreement before the final inspection.
(b) The administrator shall inform the applicant whether the application and supporting materials are approved or disapproved.
(c) If the application or supporting materials are disapproved, the administrator shall notify the applicant of such fact in writing. The applicant may then revise any item not meeting the requirements hereof and resubmit the same for the administrator to again consider and either approve or disapprove.
(d) If the application and supporting materials are approved, the City may issue the associated land disturbance permit or building permit, provided all other legal requirements for the issuance of such permits have been met. The stormwater management plan included in such applications becomes the approved stormwater management plan.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 2, 11-18-2020)
